reviews.scope: Recognizing undefined tangent angles and basic anchor values before full branch analysis.
reviews.reason: Identifying where cosine vanishes and evaluating basic values like tan 0 and tan 45 degrees introduces tangent domain exclusions and anchor points before studying open continuity branches, period pi, strict monotonicity, and pole limits.
reviews.counterexample: One can define tan(t)=sin(t)/cos(t) directly in radians and derive its poles, period, and branch behavior from sine and cosine properties without prior degree-based special-angle drills.

reviews.scope: Locating poles and endpoint behavior in the unit-circle quotient proof of tangent branches.
reviews.reason: In the unit-circle quotient derivation, defining sine and cosine as terminal-point coordinates and evaluating axial angles at 0 and 90 degrees locates the cosine zeros that form tangent poles and anchors branch behavior.
reviews.counterexample: Tangent poles, continuity branches, and monotonicity can instead be derived from the geometric tangent-line construction at x=1 or from analytic wave properties of sine and cosine.

reviews.scope: Extending principal-branch quotient properties to all branches via pi-shift reduction formulas.
reviews.reason: In the unit-circle quotient proof, reduction formulas for angles shifted by pi show that sine and cosine both negate, proving tan(t+pi)=tan(t) and extending principal-branch continuity, monotonicity, and pole limits to every branch.
reviews.counterexample: Period pi and branch repetition can be seen geometrically from antipodal unit-circle rays having identical slope y/x or identical intersection with the tangent line x=1.

reviews.scope: Proving strict branch increase via the sine-difference identity on quotient differences.
reviews.reason: In the algebraic quotient proof of branch monotonicity, the sine-difference identity rewrites tan(v)-tan(u) as sin(v-u)/(cos(u)*cos(v)), reducing strict increase on an open branch to checking factor signs.
reviews.counterexample: Strict increase on (-pi/2,pi/2) can be proved without angle-subtraction identities by differentiating tan(t) to get sec^2(t)>0, using the geometric tangent line, or combining monotone positive sine and cosine on [0,pi/2) with oddness.

reviews.scope: Determining quotient-difference positivity and pole limit signs via quadrant sign rules.
reviews.reason: In the unit-circle quotient proof, quadrant sign rules and axial values show cos(u)>0, cos(v)>0 on (-pi/2,pi/2) and sin(v-u)>0 for 0<v-u<pi, proving tan(v)-tan(u)>0 and fixing one-sided pole signs.
reviews.counterexample: Branch monotonicity and one-sided unbounded signs can instead be read directly from the geometric tangent line at x=1 or from calculus and the graphs of sine and cosine.
